ingredients.name: Prawns (medium to large)
ingredients.notes: peeled and deveined; leave tails on for presentation if desired

ingredients.name: Chilli powder
ingredients.notes: for the marinade; use Kashmiri for colour + mild heat, or cayenne for more heat

ingredients.name: Curry leaves
ingredients.notes: 2 sprigs; a generous amount is important to the dish's character

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: large, cut into thick wedges; kept crunchy

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.notes: cut into wedges; added at the end

ingredients.name: Tomato ketchup
ingredients.notes: optional; for the semi-devilled version; omit for the pure tempered style

ingredients.name: Roasted Sri Lankan curry powder
ingredients.notes: scattered at the very end for aroma

steps.instruction: Peel and devein the prawns. Marinate with turmeric, chilli powder, black pepper, lime juice, and salt. Mix well and set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a wide wok or flat pan over high heat. When smoking, add the curry leaves -- they will crackle loudly and spit. Stand back and let them crisp up for about 30 seconds.
Add the garlic, ginger, and green chillies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds on high heat.

Add the marinated prawns in a single layer. Sear without stirring for 1 minute, then flip and cook for another 30-60 seconds on the other side. The prawns should turn pink and just curl into a C shape -- do not overcook or they will turn rubbery. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the onion wedges and banana peppers. Stir-fry over high heat for 1-2 minutes, keeping them crunchy.
If making the semi-devilled version, add the ketchup and soy sauce now and toss to coat the vegetables.
Return the seared prawns to the pan. Add the tomato wedges. Toss everything together over high heat for 1 minute until everything is combined and heated through.
Sprinkle the roasted curry powder over the top and give one final toss. Serve immediately -- prawns toughen quickly if left to sit. Serve with plain rice, string hoppers, or godamba roti.

source_site: hungrylankan.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, loveandotherspices.com, spiceupthecurry.com, the-hungrykat.blogspot.com, srilankanrecipes.info, theflavorbender.com, and ralahami.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 8+ independent sources; strong agreement on the marinate-then-sear-then-toss technique and the non-negotiable curry leaf temper
notes: Isso theldala (tempered prawns) is the most commonly made prawn dish in Sri Lankan home kitchens -- simpler and faster than the wet prawn curry (sl_004) or the elaborate Publis Silva devilled prawns (sl_005), and eaten more frequently as an everyday dish. Two sub-styles exist and are documented: the pure tempered style (this entry's main method, using only spices, onion, curry leaves, and lime) and the semi-devilled style (which adds ketchup and soy sauce for a glossy red-brown sauce, as in sl_032 devilled chicken). This entry documents both as optional variants. The most critical technique point is not overcooking the prawns -- they cook in under 3 minutes total and turn rubbery almost instantly if left on heat too long. The test: when they curl into a C-shape and turn fully pink, they are done; if they curl into a tight O-shape, they are overcooked. This is the 100th and final recipe in the SL-Cook100 dataset.
